elements.quote: Prognostic value of procalcitonin in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and metaanalysis
elements.reason: The report is identified as a systematic review and meta-analysis in the title/citation, satisfying PRISMA-A item 1 which is part of the abstract checklist.

elements.quote: We included studies with patients hospitalized for AECOPD, which assessed procalcitonin levels and reported on the association between procalcitonin and mortality.
elements.reason: The objective (association between procalcitonin and mortality in AECOPD) is implied through inclusion wording but is not stated as an explicit objective or review question.

elements.quote: We included studies with patients hospitalized for AECOPD, which assessed procalcitonin levels and reported on the association between procalcitonin and mortality.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria are given in the abstract, but no explicit exclusion criteria are stated there.

elements.quote: Database including PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to find relevant trials.
elements.reason: Information sources are identified, but the abstract does not report when each source was last searched.
The abstract does not describe any risk of bias assessment method; NOS assessment appears only in the main Methods (text_12).
The abstract does not describe methods of presenting or synthesizing results (e.g., pooling methods); these appear only in the main Statistical Analysis section (text_13).

elements.quote: Fourteen trials involving 2983 patients were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (14) and participants (2983).

elements.quote: subgroup analysis showed PCT levels are indeed associated with an increased risk of mortality in mild to moderate AECOPD(RR 1.74, 95%CI 1.11-2.73). Deceased patients had significantly higher PCT levels, compared to survivors (MD 0.61, 95%CI 0.30-0.92). In PCT positive group, there was a significant increase in all-cause mortality(OR 3.21, 95%CI 1.84-5.61).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes with effect estimates.

elements.quote: We found PCT levels in patients hospitalized for AECOPD are not associated with increased risk of mortality (RR 1.03, 95%CI 0.99-1.08).
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Deceased patients had significantly higher PCT levels, compared to survivors (MD 0.61, 95%CI 0.30-0.92). In PCT positive group, there was a significant increase in all-cause mortality(OR 3.21, 95%CI 1.84-5.61).
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group is favored (deceased had higher PCT; PCT-positive group had higher mortality).
The abstract does not mention limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: We found PCT levels in patients hospitalized for AECOPD are not associated with increased risk of mortality (RR 1.03, 95%CI 0.99-1.08).
elements.reason: The abstract states the main findings but provides little general interpretation of their meaning or implications.
The abstract does not state the funding source for the review.
Registration (PROSPERO CRD42020158430) is reported only in the main Methods (text_8), not in the abstract.

elements.quote: Numerous investigations have been conducted to ascertain the prognostic indicators of mortality in patients with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD)... However, there is little information about the relationship between biomarkers and death in COPD.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes current knowledge (known clinical prognostic factors) and identifies the key uncertainty (little information on biomarkers and death in COPD).

elements.quote: Given above, effective biomarkers are sought for determining the acute attack frequency, length of hospitalization, severity of morbidity, and mortality... Therefore, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the value of procalcitonin in predict mortality among patients hospitalized for AECOPD.
elements.reason: The need for the review is explicitly explained: effective biomarkers are needed, motivating the systematic review of PCT for predicting mortality in AECOPD.

elements.quote: Therefore, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the value of procalcitonin in predict mortality among patients hospitalized for AECOPD.
elements.reason: The Introduction does not mention any existing similar systematic reviews; no prior review is cited, so there is no evidence that an update/replication justification is required.

elements.quote: we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the value of procalcitonin in predict mortality
elements.reason: This is a prognostic (biomarker) review, not a review of intervention effects, so a mechanism-of-action description is not required.

elements.quote: we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the value of procalcitonin in predict mortality among patients hospitalized for AECOPD
elements.reason: The review addresses a prognostic biomarker, not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model is not applicable.

No retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s). The title implies the topic, and text_4 describes eligibility criteria, but neither constitutes an explicit objectives statement.
This is a review of prognostic value (procalcitonin and mortality in AECOPD), not a review of intervention effects, so PICO-formatted planned comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Studies fulfilling the following selection criteria were included in this meta-analysis: (1) the type of study design was observational research, (2) the relationship between procalcitonin and mortality in patients with AECOPD, (3) diagnosis of COPD based on guidelines from the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD). Reviews, case reports, conference abstracts, and animal experiments were excluded.
elements.reason: Eligible designs (observational), population (AECOPD patients, GOLD-diagnosed), and outcome (PCT-mortality relationship) are specified, along with exclusions.

elements.quote: for articles published up to October 2023 in any language. ... Reviews, case reports, conference abstracts, and animal experiments were excluded.
elements.reason: Dissemination date (up to October 2023), language (any), and publication status (conference abstracts excluded) are specified.

elements.quote: Reviews, case reports, conference abstracts, and animal experiments were excluded.
elements.reason: The flow diagram notes '4 with missing information' among exclusions, but the review never distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Eight studies reported the ability of PCT predicts mortality in AECOPD. Five studies compared mortality according to PCT levels. And four studies compared PCT levels between survivors and deceased.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (prediction of mortality, mortality by PCT level, PCT levels in survivors vs deceased; plus mild-to-moderate vs severe subgroup) are described, but they are not explicitly linked to predefined comparisons in the review objectives.

elements.quote: If multiple studies used the same patient sample, the most recent or informative article was included.
elements.reason: A rationale is given for handling duplicate samples, but no rationales are provided for other notable restrictions such as limiting to observational designs or excluding reviews and case reports.

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic search of the PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library databases for articles published up to October 2023 in any language.
elements.reason: The last search date/coverage is reported as 'up to October 2023' for all databases searched.

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic search of the PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library databases for articles published up to October 2023 in any language.
elements.reason: Database names and coverage dates ('up to October 2023') are reported, but the search interface/platform for each database is not specified.

elements.quote: Database including PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to find relevant trials.
elements.reason: The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials is named, and the coverage date 'up to October 2023' (text_9) applies, but no register-specific date restrictions are explicitly reported.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources were reported as searched.

elements.quote: Additional data sources were examined, including conference proceedings and the reference lists of the relevant studies.
elements.reason: Reference lists of relevant (included) studies were specified as an additional information source.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.

elements.quote: Additional data sources were examined, including conference proceedings and the reference lists of the relevant studies.
elements.reason: Conference proceedings are mentioned as a source, but dates covered and search methods for them are not reported.

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic search of the PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library databases for articles published up to October 2023 in any language. The search strategies were as follows: (COPD or 'chronic obstructive pulmonary disease' or 'chronic airflow obstruction' or 'chronic obstructive airway disease' or 'chronic obstructive lung disease') and (procalcitonin or PCT or pro-calcitonin or 'calcitonin precursor polyprotein' or 'calcitonin 1' or 'calcitonin related polypeptide alpha') (S1 Table).
elements.reason: Full search strings are reported for all three databases (PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library), with the complete strategy also provided in S1 Table.

elements.quote: for articles published up to October 2023 in any language

No published search approaches, filters, or hedge citations or adaptations are reported.

elements.quote: Two reviewers (Lin C and Li G) independently performed the search strategy and evaluated the studies.
elements.reason: Independence is explicitly stated for study evaluation/screening.

elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via third reviewer is described.

elements.reason: Contacting study investigators for additional details is reported.
No evidence of non-English records requiring translation; search stated 'in any language' but no translation process reported or needed per evidence.

elements.quote: Two authors (Lin C and Li G) independently reviewed the full manuscripts of eligible trails
elements.reason: Independent data extraction by the two reviewers is explicitly reported.

elements.quote: We included studies with patients hospitalized for AECOPD, which assessed procalcitonin levels and reported on the association between procalcitonin and mortality.
elements.reason: The outcomes (mortality, and PCT levels/mortality comparison) are identifiable from eligibility criteria and analyses, but outcomes are not explicitly listed and defined in the Data Extraction section; the extraction items listed are study characteristics (author, year, design, etc.), not outcome definitions.

elements.reason: The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
No process for selecting which compatible results to collect is described in the retrieved evidence.

No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported or implied in the retrieved evidence; a published PROSPERO protocol exists (CRD42020158430) but no deviations are described.
No changes to processes for selecting results within outcome domains are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.reason: The data items sought are explicitly listed, and Table 1 (table_0) shows these characteristics for each included study.

elements.quote: The 9-point NOS contains three items: selection (0-4), comparability (0-2), and exposure/outcome (0-3) (S4 Table)
elements.reason: The domains/items of the NOS and their scoring ranges are specified, with reference to S4 Table.

elements.quote: Studies that scored over 7 points on the NOS were deemed to be of high quality
elements.reason: A threshold-based overall quality judgement rule is reported, but only a 'high quality' category is defined; no full set of overall risk-of-bias judgement categories/rules is given.
No evidence of adaptations to the NOS; the standard tool appears to be used as-is.

elements.quote: two independent authors (Lin C and Li G) scored the studies... Any disagreement was resolved via the evaluation of a third reviewer (Pang Q)
elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two), independence, and disagreement-resolution via a third reviewer are reported.
No evidence that risk-of-bias information was sought from study investigators; this process does not appear to have been undertaken.

elements.quote: Continuous variables were pooled as mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) using inverse variance method. Mortality was analyzed using the Mantel-Haenszel (M-H) method to calculate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
elements.reason: The Statistical Analysis section specifies effect measures for each outcome type: MD for continuous variables, OR via Mantel-Haenszel for mortality, and log ORs from Cox models via generic inverse variance for PCT predicting mortality. Results also report RR and HR (text_14, text_5).

No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (e.g., clinically important differences) or their rationale are reported; only statistical significance (P<0.05) and heterogeneity thresholds (I2>50%) are given, which do not address effect size interpretation.

No methods for re-expressing synthesized results in another effect measure are described. The conversion of Cox regression results to log ORs is described as data extraction, not re-expression of pooled results.
The choice of effect measures (OR, MD, RR, HR) is stated but no justification for selecting these measures is provided.

elements.quote: Eight studies reported the ability of PCT predicts mortality in AECOPD. Five studies compared mortality according to PCT levels. And four studies compared PCT levels between survivors and deceased.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates which studies contributed to each of the three syntheses (prediction of mortality, mortality by PCT levels, PCT levels in survivors vs deceased) and describes the general study selection and data extraction processes, but it does not explicitly describe the processes used to decide study eligibility for each synthesis (e.g., tabulating characteristics against planned synthesis groups).

elements.quote: The estimates of log ORs and standard errors have been obtained from the results of Cox proportional hazards regression models of the included studies. ... Continuous variables were pooled as mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) using inverse variance method. Mortality was analyzed using the Mantel-Haenszel (M-H) method to calculate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI). The outcome measure was assessed in an intention-to-treat (ITT) manner.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data conversions and preparation for synthesis (log OR transformation from Cox models, MD/OR calculations, ITT assessment), but does not describe handling of missing summary statistics or other missing data preparation methods.
Tables exist (Table 1, S2-S4 Tables) but the Methods section never describes the tabular structures used to display results or the data included in them.

Forest plots appear in the Results (e.g., Fig 5), but the Methods do not describe the graphical methods used to display results; the RevMan software mention does not explicitly describe graphical display methods.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs (e.g., Table 1 ordered by year, forest plots by weight) is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Fig 5. Meta-analysis of studies compared PCT levels between survivors and deaths.
elements.reason: The displays used are standard meta-analytic forest plots and standard tables; no non-standard graphs are used, so no rationale for non-standard graphs is required.

elements.quote: All data analyses were performed using the RevMan(v 5.3) software.
elements.reason: Software and version (RevMan v5.3) explicitly reported.
Meta-analysis was performed, so no alternative synthesis method needed.

elements.quote: Considering the high likelihood of between-study variance, we used a random effect model.
elements.reason: Random-effects model reported with rationale.

elements.quote: combined using the generic inverse variance method... Mortality was analyzed using the Mantel-Haenszel (M-H) method to calculate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
elements.reason: Statistical methods (inverse variance, Mantel-Haenszel) described.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity among studies was assessed by Cochrane Q and I 2 statistics, I 2 values of more than 50% were considered to represent significant heterogeneity
elements.reason: Heterogeneity assessment method and threshold reported.
Random-effects model used but the between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird) is not reported.
Method for calculating confidence intervals for the summary effect is not specified.
No additional random-effects implementation details reported.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed.
Two studies used the same sample [15, 23], but no method for handling statistical dependency among estimates is described.
No evidence that planned syntheses were judged impossible or inappropriate; all planned syntheses appear to have been conducted.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was performed based on the severity of disease. Severe cases are defined as requiring intubation or mechanical ventilation, and others as mild to moderate.
elements.reason: Methods section explicitly describes subgroup analysis by disease severity to explore heterogeneity.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was performed based on the severity of disease. Severe cases are defined as requiring intubation or mechanical ventilation, and others as mild to moderate.
elements.reason: Factor (severity) and levels (severe vs mild to moderate) are reported, but no expected direction of effect modification is stated.
No statement on whether subgroup analyses used study-level variables or within-study contrasts.

No existing reporting-bias/missing-result assessment tool was used, so there are no domains or overall judgement process to report.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are reported; no such tool was used.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is described or referenced.

elements.quote: A search of databases revealed a total of 1447 studies, after removal of duplicates there were 1225 studies left for analysis. During the screening process, 1189 studies were eliminated for various reasons based on the title and abstract.
elements.reason: Numbers identified (1447), duplicates removed (to 1225), screened (1225), and excluded at title/abstract screening (1189) are reported in text and in the Fig 1 flow diagram.

elements.reason: The Fig 1 flow diagram (visible in image attached to text_9) reports full-text articles assessed (36) and exclusions with reasons (16 total: 13 did not meet criteria, 5 conference abstract, 4 missing information). Note the stated reasons sum to 22, exceeding n=16, a minor internal inconsistency, but the required elements are reported.

elements.quote: Subsequently, fourteen studies were included in our analysis [15-26], and two [15, 23] of which used the same sample.
